data_output.description: data.py must preserve the existing encoded interface: encoded[split] is (features, labels, user_ids), where features is int32 shape [N,2] containing offset-encoded user and video IDs, labels is float32 shape [N], user_ids preserves validation-row order, and dimension is the total encoded ID dimension including unknown buckets. train.py must emit an NPZ containing exactly row_ids and scores; row_ids must be int64 canonical validation positions arange(N), and scores must be a finite one-dimensional array of length N aligned to those rows.

model_input.description: Model(dimension, learning_rate, l2) receives the encoded feature matrix with column 0 as the user global ID and column 1 as the video global ID. It must expose logits(features), step(features, labels), predict(features, batch_size), state(), and load_state(state). Its score must be user_bias + video_bias + dot(user_embedding, video_embedding), with embedding dimension 32, pointwise BCE-compatible sigmoid gradients, finite predictions, and unchanged trainer compatibility.
